mission_work_items.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
mission_work_items.effects: Read only. Does not create or schedule WorkItems.
mission_work_items.notes: mission_id is the required opaque public Mission identifier. The Mission must exist; unknown IDs return resource-not-found. At most 25 items, ordered by insertion time and WorkItem ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri.
mission_work_items.result: The first custode.work_item.list.v1 page restricted to one Mission; items use the same summary contract as work_items.

mission_work_items_page.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
mission_work_items_page.effects: Read only. Does not change authoritative application state.
mission_work_items_page.notes: mission_id is the required opaque public Mission identifier; cursor is a required token from that Mission's preceding WorkItem page. Percent-encode each segment or follow page.next_uri. Unknown Mission returns resource-not-found. A cursor from another Mission or global WorkItem list returns invalid-params. At most 25 items.
mission_work_items_page.result: A continuation custode.work_item.list.v1 page restricted to the named Mission.

work_attention_page.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_attention_page.effects: Read only. Does not acknowledge or resolve obligations.
work_attention_page.notes: cursor is the required opaque token from a preceding Attention page. Invalid cursors return invalid-params. At most 25 items. Attention is recomputed on each read, so continuation is not a frozen snapshot of obligations. Legacy asks and gates are included.
work_attention_page.result: A continuation custode.attention.list.v1 page of derived operator obligations, with the same item and projection fields as work_attention.

work_events_page.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_events_page.effects: Read only. Does not append or replay events.
work_events_page.notes: cursor is the required opaque token from a preceding global WorkEvent page. WorkItem-scoped event cursors cannot be reused here. Invalid or cross-scope cursors return invalid-params. At most 25 events.
work_events_page.result: A continuation custode.work_event.list.v1 page across all WorkItems.

work_item_artifacts.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_item_artifacts.effects: Read only. Reads artifact metadata; does not open, download, validate, or mutate the artifact bytes at the location.
work_item_artifacts.notes: work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found. Includes all stored artifacts, including expired records, unlike relevant_artifacts in WorkItem summaries. At most 25 items ordered by insertion time and artifact ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri.
work_item_artifacts.result: A custode.artifact.list.v1 page of custode.artifact.v1 metadata, including ID/kind/producer, external identity, digest/media type, location/size, retention/expiry/provenance, parent IDs, and timestamps.

work_item_artifacts_page.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_item_artifacts_page.effects: Read only. Does not read or modify artifact bytes or authoritative state.
work_item_artifacts_page.notes: work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier; cursor is a required continuation token from that same WorkItem's artifact collection. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found. Invalid or cross-scope cursor returns invalid-params. At most 25 metadata records.
work_item_artifacts_page.result: A continuation custode.artifact.list.v1 metadata page for the WorkItem.

work_item_attempt.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_item_attempt.effects: Read only. Does not create, resume, or run an Attempt.
work_item_attempt.notes: work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found; an existing WorkItem without an Attempt returns attempt=null. Selects the explicitly active Attempt if set, otherwise the newest logical Attempt. Check attempt.active before treating it as live execution.
work_item_attempt.result: A custode.work_item.current_attempt.v1 object containing mission_id, work_item_id, a nullable detailed attempt, and links. Attempt details include provider/profile, state/timing, context IDs/digest, provenance/usage/continuation, job/workflow identifiers, outcome and errors.

work_item_detail.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_item_detail.effects: Read only. Does not advance work, start an Attempt, or resolve a gate.
work_item_detail.notes: work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier. Unknown IDs return resource-not-found. State and workflow phase have different meanings and remain separate. relevant_artifacts excludes expired records; the dedicated artifact collection includes them.
work_item_detail.result: A custode.work_item.detail.v1 object. Adds objective/acceptance criteria, source/external key/policy, active Attempt/call IDs, waiting/blocked conditions, outcome and terminal timestamps, full nested current Attempt/open gates/relevant artifacts, relationship IDs, and navigation links to the summary fields.

work_item_events.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_item_events.effects: Read only. Does not append, replay, or modify events.
work_item_events.notes: work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found. At most 25 events ordered by insertion time and event ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri. This is kernel event history, not provider conversation history.
work_item_events.result: The first custode.work_event.list.v1 page restricted to the WorkItem's transition and process history.

work_item_events_page.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_item_events_page.effects: Read only. Does not append, replay, or modify events.
work_item_events_page.notes: work_item_id is the required opaque public WorkItem identifier; cursor is a required token from that WorkItem's preceding event page. Unknown WorkItem returns resource-not-found. Invalid or wrong-scope cursor returns invalid-params. At most 25 events.
work_item_events_page.result: A continuation custode.work_event.list.v1 page restricted to the WorkItem.

work_items_page.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_items_page.effects: Read only. Does not change authoritative application state.
work_items_page.notes: cursor is a required opaque token from a preceding global WorkItem page. It cannot be reused from a Mission-scoped list. Percent-encode it or follow page.next_uri. Invalid cursors return invalid-params. At most 25 items.
work_items_page.result: A continuation custode.work_item.list.v1 page across all Missions.

work_mission_detail.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_mission_detail.effects: Read only. Does not create or modify the Mission or its related records.
work_mission_detail.notes: mission_id is the required opaque public Mission identifier, not a database row number. Percent-encode it as one path segment. Unknown IDs return resource-not-found. Mission records can be compatibility projections for active routines while work-kernel intake is frozen.
work_mission_detail.result: A custode.mission.detail.v1 object: summary fields plus retention, metadata, relationship IDs for WorkItems/Attempts/calls/gates/artifacts/events, and self/work_items links.

work_missions_page.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator; other identities receive resource-not-found.
work_missions_page.effects: Read only. Does not change authoritative application state.
work_missions_page.notes: cursor is the required opaque continuation token from the preceding Mission page. Percent-encode the segment or use page.next_uri directly. At most 25 items. Invalid or wrong-collection cursors return invalid-params.
work_missions_page.result: The next custode.mission.list.v1 page with the same item and navigation shape as work_missions.

work_attention.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator. Other identities do not discover the resource and reads return resource-not-found.
work_attention.effects: Read only. Derives obligations afresh; does not acknowledge, resolve, or otherwise mutate them.
work_attention.notes: No arguments. At most 25 items; severity descending, raised time ascending, then attention key ascending. Includes open work gates, blocked WorkItems, latest failed/stale operation calls, and open legacy asks/gates. This is not the list_attention fleet projection. Legacy-agent items can have null resource links. Resolve the source state to remove an obligation.
work_attention.result: A custode.attention.list.v1 page of custode.attention.item.v1 obligations. Items contain subject, reason/evidence, severity/age, owner, authoritative source, and links. The page declares projection.derived=true and projection.independently_mutable=false.

work_events.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator. Other identities do not discover the resource and reads return resource-not-found.
work_events.effects: Read only. Does not append events, replay work, or change authoritative application state.
work_events.notes: No arguments. First global page of append-only work-kernel history, at most 25 items; insertion time and event ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri. This is not the routine activity feed.
work_events.result: A custode.work_event.list.v1 page of custode.work_event.v1 events. Events include actor/operation, before and after state/phase/version, evidence, call/gate and correlation/causation IDs, parent IDs, and timestamp.

work_items.access: Main endpoint only. Authenticated operator. Other identities do not discover the resource and reads return resource-not-found.
work_items.effects: Read only. Does not advance WorkItems, run Attempts, or change authoritative application state.
work_items.notes: No arguments. First global page, at most 25 items, ordered by insertion time then WorkItem ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri. This is the frozen work-kernel model, not the routine roster or current agent execution list.
work_items.result: A custode.work_item.list.v1 page of custode.work_item.summary.v1 items across Missions. Includes state and workflow phase separately, priority/version, current Attempt, open gates, unexpired relevant artifacts, last transition, compatibility metadata, and timestamps.

work_missions.access: Main endpoint only. Listed and readable for an authenticated operator; routine and sub-agent identities see no resource and reads return resource-not-found.
work_missions.effects: Read only. Computes a projection from stored records; does not create Missions, schedule work, or change authoritative application state.
work_missions.notes: No arguments. First page, at most 25 items. Ordered by insertion time and Mission ID ascending. Follow page.next_uri. The work-kernel intake is frozen, but compatibility Mission records for active routines can still exist.
work_missions.result: A custode.mission.list.v1 page of custode.mission.summary.v1 items. Summaries include identity, purpose, lifecycle/status, targets, policy/budget/context references, work counts by state, last transition, compatibility metadata, and timestamps.

add_routine.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. A human operator may write directly; a caretaker must also have a live human-approved continuation whose action class is roster. Specialists and temporary agents are refused before configuration changes.
add_routine.effects: Appends configuration, reloads the live roster and records a feed entry. The routine becomes beatable immediately and eligible for scheduling. Also mints credentials, writes the routine MCP config, initializes its workspace and starts repository service when configured.
add_routine.notes: id is required. provider is claude or codex and defaults to claude. Intended flow is preview, human approval, then add. The tool's current external-tag policy check allows the write; it does not impose a separate human-only restriction. No idempotency key; duplicate IDs are validated by the configuration writer.
add_routine.result: id, path of configuration file, live=true.
add_routine.summary: Add a routine to the configuration and live roster.

agent_history.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. A routine may read history only for a temporary agent whose durable spawn record names it as parent; the operator may read any target. Missing or reconciled records do not widen access.
agent_history.notes: last defaults to 20. The tool takes the final N history entries and renders each as printable diagnostic text with a 200-character printable-value limit. Entries are not a stable typed event protocol; no positive bound on last is declared here.
agent_history.result: agent_id and entries array of diagnostic strings, oldest first within the selected tail.
agent_history.summary: Read the recent tail of an agent event history.

agent_status.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. A routine may inspect only a temporary agent whose durable spawn record names it as parent; the operator may inspect any target. Missing or reconciled records do not widen access.
agent_status.effects: None; reads agent lifecycle, pending inbox wake and Custode-owned conversation-arc state.
agent_status.notes: agent_id is required. detail is diagnostic text and can carry pending gate information; no structured action object is guaranteed. pending_wake is null when no durable inbox wake remains. When present it explains the coalesced note count, delivery state, timing and current blocker; reading it does not deliver or clear the wake. pending_wake.spend_override is true when a manual resume authorized that wake past the daily spend rail. It does not replace blocked_by, which continues to report the current delivery blocker. conversation is the durable read model shared with LiveView. Provider session ids are opaque, host-local acceleration handles and may be null.
agent_status.result: All states: agent_id, state, pending_wake and conversation with current plus active arcs. pending_wake is null or contains wake_id, reason, state, note_count, first_note_at, last_note_at, due_at, blocked_by, spend_override and claimed_at. A current conversation arc names its logical and provider arc ids, kind, provider, optional provider_session_id, host/workspace/config identity, decision, reason, outcome and timestamps. Running agents also return detail, turns, cost_usd, legacy default session_id, active_arc_id and the wrapper's current or latest continuation.
agent_status.summary: Inspect one agent, its pending inbox wake and durable conversation arc.

answer_ask.access: Main endpoint capability: human operator only. Routines and temporary agents are refused. The handler repeats the human-operator check.
answer_ask.effects: Closes an open ask, records the answer and feed event, and attempts best-effort delivery as a routine inbox note.
answer_ask.notes: ask_id and a nonblank answer are required. Missing or already-resolved asks produce a tool error. An identity without a configured routine still has its ask closed even though no inbox delivery is possible; success is not a recipient-processing receipt.
answer_ask.summary: Answer a non-blocking question and notify its agent.

approve_action.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. A routine may approve only a temporary agent whose durable spawn record names it as parent and may never decide a configured routine's gate. The operator may override target scope. Missing or reconciled records do not widen access.
approve_action.effects: Resolves an approval gate and starts its approved continuation; records decision actor and transport.
approve_action.notes: agent_id and action_id are required. Obtain the current action ID from status/await/gates. Success means the continuation is processing, not that work completed. A durable gate whose provider action no longer exists is requeued for a configured routine (or orphaned for a temporary agent) and returns a rehydration_required isError tool result over HTTP 200. A live enqueue refusal remains open and retryable. Retrying an already-approved action succeeds idempotently with already_applied=true and cannot enqueue a second continuation; a different recorded outcome or unknown action remains an error.
approve_action.result: agent_id and approved action_id; already_applied=true only when the same approval had already succeeded.
approve_action.summary: Approve an agent action awaiting a decision.

ask_operator.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
ask_operator.effects: Stores an open question for the operator without pausing the current turn. A future answer arrives as an inbox note.
ask_operator.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. question is runtime-required despite not being schema-required. detail is optional. Suggested replies are trimmed, deduplicated, limited to 3, and blank or over-120-character replies are discarded. The configured open-ask cap defaults to 2 per identity. This is not permission approval. Retrying can create another ask until the cap is reached.
ask_operator.result: ask_id, status and note confirming non-blocking filing.
ask_operator.summary: Ask a non-blocking question whose answer will arrive later.

await_agent.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. A routine may await only a temporary agent whose durable spawn record names it as parent; the operator may await any target. Missing or reconciled records do not widen access.
await_agent.effects: None; blocks the request while waiting.
await_agent.notes: message_id is optional during migration and is authoritative for new clients. With message_id, timeout_ms defaults to 60000, is clamped to 0..180000, and waits only for that durable message to reach waiting_for_input, waiting_for_approval, completed, failed or refused. The message must belong to the named agent and authenticated caller, except that the operator may inspect every caller. A timeout returns the current durable message with timed_out=true. Without message_id, legacy agent-level waiting remains: settled states include idle, awaiting_permission, waiting_for_user, paused and offline, and last_result may belong to an earlier turn.
await_agent.result: With message_id: the exact durable message receipt (message_id, target, caller provenance, status, delivery, provider turn identity, continuation link, detail, result, error and timestamps), plus agent_id and timed_out. Without it: agent_id, state, detail, timed_out and last_result.
await_agent.summary: Wait for one exact message, or use legacy agent-level waiting.

beat.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. The shared operator action repeats that boundary, so specialists, temporary agents and alternate clients are refused before a tick is queued.
beat.effects: Queues an out-of-schedule routine sweep through the usual lifecycle policy, potentially starting an offline agent.
beat.notes: agent_id is required and must be a known routine. Success reports scheduling, not run admission or completion. Busy/paused/lifecycle policy can still affect execution. No idempotency key is exposed.
beat.summary: Schedule an immediate sweep of a configured routine.

compact_journal.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
compact_journal.effects: Marks all currently live entries compacted and inserts a new summary in one transaction; regenerates views and notifies. Originals remain temporarily readable until retirement.
compact_journal.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. summary is runtime-required despite optional discovery schema. This is an authored distillation, not automatic summarization. Repeating it creates another summary and compacts the previous summary too.
compact_journal.result: summarized count of previously live entries.
compact_journal.summary: Replace the live journal view with an authored summary.

define_profile.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. A human operator may write directly; a caretaker must also have a live human-approved continuation whose action class is roster. Specialists and temporary agents are refused before configuration changes.
define_profile.effects: Writes a profile, reloads the roster and records a feed entry. Routines can inherit it immediately.
define_profile.notes: name is required. provider is claude or codex and becomes the default provider for wearers. Intended flow requires preview and human approval of dangerous grants. approve_bypass_permissions=false is omitted. No restart is required for configuration reload; this is not a runtime permission revocation protocol for an in-flight turn.
define_profile.result: name, configuration path, grants and live=true.

digest.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
digest.notes: days defaults to 1 at the MCP boundary and must be a positive integer for the underlying builder, despite no schema range. The window is based on UTC days. markdown defaults false. Summary includes observed records, not a guarantee of exhaustive external activity.
digest.result: Default: since, window_days, spend, sweeps, gates, failures, suggestions and anomalies. With markdown=true: an object containing markdown text.
digest.summary: Summarize fleet activity over a recent window.

dismiss_ask.access: Main endpoint capability: human operator only. Routines and temporary agents are refused. The handler repeats the human-operator check.
dismiss_ask.effects: Closes an open ask and records an optional reason without answering it or sending an inbox note.
dismiss_ask.notes: ask_id is required. reason is optional. Missing or already-resolved asks produce a tool error. This is not the rejection of an approval gate.
dismiss_ask.summary: Close a non-blocking question without sending an answer.

drain.access: Main endpoint capability: human operator only. The shared operator action repeats the human-only boundary and refuses every routine and temporary agent before pausing queues.
drain.effects: Closes work admission, pauses execution queues and begins a background wait. Stops the server after executing jobs finish; a timeout leaves queues paused and emits a feed event.
drain.notes: timeout_ms is optional; omission means unbounded waiting. The response confirms drain admission, not server shutdown. Existing executing jobs may continue. Observe feed/executing_turns for progress. On timeout, queue resumption is a separate recovery action, not automatic.
drain.result: draining=true, executing count and explanatory note.
drain.summary: Stop admitting work and shut down after executing jobs finish.

drop_note.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. The shared operator action repeats that boundary, so specialists, temporary agents and alternate clients are refused before a note is written.
drop_note.effects: Writes a routine inbox note and triggers its debounced on_note event policy, which can cause a sweep. Records an inbox feed event.
drop_note.notes: agent_id and content are required. name defaults to note-<UTC timestamp to seconds>.md. File writing and kickoff are part of this operation; a raw file write is not equivalent. Reusing a name can overwrite the same path; there is no dedicated idempotency key. The current name input is joined to the inbox path without a basename check; callers should pass a simple filename. Kickoff failure is logged and does not turn a successful file write into a tool error.
drop_note.summary: Write a routine inbox note and trigger its note-arrival policy.

executing_turns.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
executing_turns.notes: No arguments. The current query returns all jobs whose state is executing, not only jobs positively identified as agent turns. It is the drain's current job inventory, not an agent-to-turn correlation API.
executing_turns.result: executing array of id, queue and worker. A Custode.OneShotJob entry also carries its resolved max_turns.
executing_turns.summary: Read the currently executing job inventory used by drain.

feed_tail.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
feed_tail.notes: agent_id optionally filters; n defaults to 20 with no declared positive range. Feed records are event-specific and can carry different fields.
feed_tail.summary: Read recent fleet activity feed entries.

forget.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine; memory endpoint capability: temporary agent. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
forget.effects: Deletes persistent memory for the identity/key.
forget.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. key is runtime-required despite optional discovery schema. Deleting an absent key is successful. There is no undo or returned previous value.
forget.summary: Delete a persistent fact by key.

inbox_list.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Any authenticated caller reaching this tool may read another configured routine's notes by ID; no self-only read guard.
inbox_list.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. Target must be a configured routine. Only inbox/*.md notes whose content does not begin FILED are returned. Distinct from list_inbox, which is the operator attention inbox.
inbox_list.result: notes array of name and content.
inbox_list.summary: Read unfiled notes in a configured routine inbox.

inbox_mark_filed.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
inbox_mark_filed.effects: Prepends a FILED date marker to an existing inbox note. Does not append journal content automatically.
inbox_mark_filed.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. name is runtime-required, must be a filename rather than a path, and must exist in the routine inbox. Caller is expected to journal relevant content first. An existing FILED prefix makes retry a no-op. Unknown routine, invalid name and file errors become tool errors.
inbox_mark_filed.summary: Mark an inbox note as already incorporated.

journal_append.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
journal_append.effects: Inserts a journal entry, regenerates journal.md/TODO.md views for a configured routine and notifies the dashboard. Database is the source of truth.
journal_append.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. body is runtime-required despite optional discovery schema; title is optional. Entries use source='sweep'. Retrying appends another entry, so this is not idempotent.

journal_read.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine; memory endpoint capability: temporary agent. Authenticated agents may read only their own journal; the operator may name another identity.
journal_read.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. limit defaults to 20 and must be an integer from 1 through 100. search is case-insensitive in title/body. live_only defaults true; false includes compacted entries until retired. Newest first, tie-broken by ID. Empty results are successful.
journal_read.result: entries array: id, title, body, inserted_at and compacted_at.
journal_read.summary: Read recent entries from the caller journal.

list_advisors.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_advisors.notes: days defaults to 30 through the advisor reader. No positive range is declared. grade distinguishes deterministic, judgment and unknown; records summarize proposal outcomes and cost.
list_advisors.result: advisors array: advisor, grade, standing, applied, settled, observing, reverted, superseded, dismissed, dismissed_by_reason, cost_usd and summary.
list_advisors.summary: Compare advisor activity, recorded outcomes and cost.

list_asks.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_asks.notes: agent_id optionally filters. Only open questions, oldest first. The response currently omits suggested replies even though ask_operator accepts them. Distinct from blocking approval/question gates.
list_asks.result: asks array: id, agent_id, question, detail and asked_at.
list_asks.summary: List open non-blocking questions for the operator.

list_attention.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_attention.notes: group optionally filters needs_you, watching, working, scheduled or quiet. Unknown group values return no matching groups rather than a validation error. Signal order is the fleet's current attention ranking.
list_attention.result: groups array, each with group and signals. Signals contain subject, kind, group, urgency, headline, detail, raised_at and resolving actions (label, op, args).
list_attention.summary: Read the fleet attention ranking grouped by need.

list_disowned.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_disowned.notes: repo optionally filters records. Newest first. No limit or pagination input.
list_disowned.result: disowned array: repo, number, disowned_by, reason and at.
list_disowned.summary: List pull requests the fleet has disowned.

list_gates.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_gates.notes: status optionally filters open, resolved, requeued or orphaned; omission includes recent gates generally. limit defaults to 20 without a schema bound. Newest first. Use action_id, not the database row ID, for approve_action/reject_action. Eligible ready_pr and merge gates enqueue a sealed review by the other provider family. Reviews are reused for an unchanged PR head and capped at three rounds per PR by default.
list_gates.result: gates array: agent_id, kind, action_id, detail, class, repo, pr_number, risk, review_state, review, status and opened_at. review is null or the other provider's head-pinned summary, typed findings and error.
list_gates.summary: Read recent blocking questions and approval gates.

list_inbox.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_inbox.effects: None; this read does not advance the operator's last-read timestamp.
list_inbox.notes: unread_only defaults false. This is the operator attention inbox, distinct from inbox_list, which reads a routine's file-based notes. Action descriptors are not a promise that each action already has a same-named MCP tool.
list_inbox.result: items array and last_read_at. Items contain kind, subject, headline, detail, at and actions (label, op, args).
list_inbox.summary: Read what the fleet has raised to the operator.

list_policies.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_policies.notes: agent_id optionally selects policies binding a known routine. A missing or unknown ID currently returns all policies rather than an unknown-routine error.
list_policies.result: policies array; each policy's applies field is 'all' or an array of selector/value objects.
list_policies.summary: Read declared policies for the fleet or a routine.

list_roles.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_roles.notes: No arguments. The role registry describes purpose, hierarchy, watch/write scope and default tool bundle. Tool exposure is separate from tool-specific runtime authorization.
list_roles.result: roles array with role metadata and grants, plus tiers.
list_roles.summary: Read role definitions, hierarchy and default grants.

list_routines.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_routines.effects: None; reads configured routines and live lifecycle status.
list_routines.notes: No arguments. Paths are expanded absolute paths. status is diagnostic text, not a portable structured lifecycle enum.
list_routines.result: Object with routines array: id, provider, cron, repo, tags, workspace, working_dir, status.
list_routines.summary: List configured routines and their current status.

list_suggestion_outcomes.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_suggestion_outcomes.notes: days defaults to 30 through the outcome reader. It is a trailing seconds-based window when supplied. No positive range is declared. Status describes recorded outcomes rather than proving that a proposal improved results.
list_suggestion_outcomes.result: decisions array: agent, advisor, field, proposed, decision, status, reason, at, observed and summary.
list_suggestion_outcomes.summary: Read what became of decisions about advisor proposals.

list_suggestions.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_suggestions.notes: No arguments. Reports unresolved proposals, not an apply/dismiss API. Proposal records can include advisor-specific fields.
list_suggestions.result: suggestions array of standing advisor proposal records.
list_suggestions.summary: Read standing proposals from fleet advisors.

list_workflows.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
list_workflows.notes: No arguments. Does not launch workflows. Catalog availability must not be interpreted as an exposed MCP launch operation or as reactivating the frozen work kernel.
list_workflows.result: workflows array containing name and, when the catalog entry resolves, stages count.
list_workflows.summary: Read the workflow catalog without launching work.

metrics.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
metrics.notes: kind is required and runtime-validated against spend, turns, gate_latency, by_model, gate_outcomes and prs_opened. days defaults to 7. gate_latency always reads the 15 most recent non-open gates and does not apply days; its empty result is gates=[] and median_minutes=0. Positive day bounds are not declared.
metrics.result: kind, days and data. spend: date-to-agent maps of usd/tokens. turns: date maps of ok/failed. gate_latency: gates array plus integer median_minutes. by_model: model maps of usd/tokens/turns/failed. gate_outcomes: agent maps of outcome counts. prs_opened: agent arrays of repo/number.
metrics.summary: Read one category of fleet measurements.

operator_bootstrap.access: Main endpoint capability: human operator only. The tool is named in no routine's exposure list, so only the operator discovers it, and the handler refuses every routine before building the result. The shared builder does not repeat the check.
operator_bootstrap.effects: None; read-only. The tool performs no file I/O and never creates the installation id. It reads the id that application boot provisioned, and fails with an installation-unavailable error when the installation is not provisioned.
operator_bootstrap.notes: No arguments. schema_version is custode.operator_bootstrap.v1. installation.id is a stable non-secret id for this instance, provisioned at boot; host is null if the hostname lookup fails and timezone is the configured fleet timezone or null. caller.transport is mcp or cli. caller.verified is true only when the router attached an authenticated identity, and false for a direct call with no request context. authority is fixed at scope all and endpoint main; tool_count is the number of tools in the tool policy, not a per-call grant. fleet.caretaker is null when no caretaker is configured. Fleet counts come from the sources the console reads: attention groups, open gates, open asks, agent lifecycle state and executing jobs. expand pairs each topic with an existing read operation; tool discovery remains authoritative for schemas. The result holds no token, filesystem path, prompt text or provider transcript.
operator_bootstrap.result: schema_version, installation (id, custode_version, host, timezone), caller (kind, id, transport, verified), authority (scope, endpoint, tool_count), fleet and expand. fleet has caretaker (id and state, or null), routines (total and by_state counts), executing_turns count, attention (total and by_group counts), open_gates and open_asks counts. expand is an array of topic and tool.
operator_bootstrap.summary: Read the first-contact brief for an operator session.

pause_agent.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. The registered shared operation repeats that boundary and refuses specialists and temporary agents.
pause_agent.effects: Requests an emergency pause, records the operation and its audit event. Resume is a separate operation.
pause_agent.notes: agent_id is required. idempotency_key is optional at the MCP boundary; omission generates a new key. Reuse one key when retrying the same logical pause. Do not assume the response reverses already completed file or remote effects.
pause_agent.summary: Emergency-pause an agent until it is resumed.

preview_profile.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
preview_profile.effects: None; validates and renders a profile preview.
preview_profile.notes: name is required. provider is claude or codex. The four approve_* inputs are a deliberately narrow Claude permission/model/worktree override surface; Codex profiles use the provider's default approved continuation arguments unless approved_args are authored in configuration. approve_bypass_permissions=false is omitted, not an explicit removal operation.
preview_profile.result: toml plus grants describing dangerous permissions carried by the proposed profile.
preview_profile.summary: Preview a reusable routine profile and its permissions.

preview_profile_edit.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
preview_profile_edit.effects: None; validates and previews the existing profile change.
preview_profile_edit.notes: name is required. provider is claude or codex. Omitted envelope fields remain unchanged; lists replace; drop removes named envelope keys and wins over supplied values. approve_* inputs build the Claude approved_args envelope; false bypass does not remove an existing grant. Inspect the preview when altering these grants. Supplying any approve_* values replaces the approved_args envelope rather than merging individual nested keys.
preview_profile_edit.result: before, after and grants for the resulting profile.
preview_profile_edit.summary: Preview edits to a reusable routine profile.

preview_routine.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
preview_routine.effects: None; renders a preview without creating or scheduling a routine.
preview_routine.notes: id is required. provider is claude or codex and defaults to claude. This creation preview checks effort but is not the complete write-time validation. Unknown profile/role values can be reported as 'unknown profile'. The workspace default is workspaces/<id>; profile and fleet defaults supply omitted settings.
preview_routine.result: toml containing the proposed routine configuration section.
preview_routine.summary: Preview the configuration for a new routine.

preview_routine_edit.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
preview_routine_edit.effects: None; validates and previews an existing routine edit.
preview_routine_edit.notes: id is required. provider is claude or codex. Omitted fields are unchanged; drop removes named overrides so inherited values can apply. Lists replace existing lists. Conflicting drop and supplied values resolve to removal. The routine ID is immutable.
preview_routine_edit.result: before and after strings containing configuration sections.
preview_routine_edit.summary: Preview a change to an existing routine.

provision_owned_checkout.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The shared operation repeats this role check.
provision_owned_checkout.effects: May create the checkouts parent directory and clone the named GitHub repository through host gh authentication into the deterministic checkouts/<routine_id> path. Records one OperationCall and a typed filesystem effect. Dry run records an OperationCall but changes no files.
provision_owned_checkout.notes: routine_id and repository owner/name are required; provisioning may run before the roster entry exists. Existing matching clones are idempotent success. Occupied, mismatched, unsafe, or unsuccessfully cloned destinations are preserved and return structured errors. Supply a stable idempotency_key when retrying one logical request.
provision_owned_checkout.result: Execution returns routine_id, repository, absolute path and status provisioned or already_provisioned. Dry run returns status=dry_run and an effect_preview naming the path and possible clone.
provision_owned_checkout.summary: Provision a routine-owned clone at its deterministic Custode path.

prompt_agent.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. A routine may prompt only a temporary agent whose durable spawn record names it as parent; the operator may message any target through the shared operator action. Missing or reconciled records do not widen access.
prompt_agent.effects: Creates a durable operator-message record, then sends or queues work exactly once for a new caller/target/idempotency tuple. For an operator, can resume a paused agent or start an offline configured routine and records activity.
prompt_agent.notes: agent_id and prompt are required. idempotency_key is optional; omission creates a new logical message, while retrying the same caller, target and key with the same prompt returns the existing receipt and duplicate=true. Reusing the key with different text is a tool error. Waiting-for-user input creates a new public message linked to the question while retaining its provider correlation; busy input queues. Operator how='started' means startup was accepted, not that execution began. A refusal before enqueue returns a durable refused receipt with delivered=false rather than losing the attempt. New clients should pass the returned message_id to await_agent.
prompt_agent.result: The durable message receipt: message_id, target and caller provenance, status, delivery path, provider and exact turn identity when known, continuation link, detail, result, error and timestamps; plus agent_id, delivered, how and duplicate.
prompt_agent.summary: Send one durable, idempotent message or answer to an agent.

recall.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine; memory endpoint capability: temporary agent. Any authenticated caller reaching this tool may read another identity's memories by ID. No self-only read guard.
recall.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. key is optional; omission returns all memory. A missing requested key is a tool error ('nothing remembered under ...'), not a null result. The endpoint's small tool set does not imply memory reads are self-only. Full-memory results are sorted by key.
recall.result: Without key: memories array of key/value. With key: key and value.
recall.summary: Read one or all persistent facts for an identity.

refresh_owned_checkout.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The shared operation repeats this role check.
refresh_owned_checkout.effects: For a configured routine using its deterministic owned checkout, may fetch origin and fast-forward the clean checked-out default branch. Records one OperationCall and a typed filesystem effect. Dry run records an OperationCall but performs no Git command.
refresh_owned_checkout.notes: routine_id is required. Existing-checkout routines are refused. The routine must be offline or idle; dirty, detached, non-default, ahead, divergent, mismatched, or unavailable checkouts are preserved and return structured errors. Command output and origin credentials are never returned. Supply a stable idempotency_key when retrying.
refresh_owned_checkout.result: Execution returns routine_id, repository, absolute path, branch, commit count and status up_to_date or fast_forwarded. Dry run returns status=dry_run and an effect_preview naming the path and possible fetch/fast-forward.
refresh_owned_checkout.summary: Safely refresh a configured routine-owned checkout.

reject_action.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. A routine may reject only a temporary agent whose durable spawn record names it as parent and may never decide a configured routine's gate. The operator may override target scope. Missing or reconciled records do not widen access.
reject_action.effects: Rejects the pending action, returns the target to idle, and records rejection feedback; feedback is standing by default.
reject_action.notes: agent_id and action_id are required. reason is optional. one_off=true makes feedback proposal-specific; omission or false makes it standing. A durable gate whose provider action no longer exists is requeued for a configured routine (or orphaned for a temporary agent) and returns a rehydration_required isError tool result over HTTP 200. Retrying an already-rejected action succeeds idempotently with already_applied=true and cannot write rejection feedback twice; a different recorded outcome or unknown action remains an error.
reject_action.result: agent_id and rejected action_id; already_applied=true only when the same rejection had already succeeded.
reject_action.summary: Reject an agent action and optionally give feedback.

remember.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine; memory endpoint capability: temporary agent. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
remember.effects: Upserts persistent memory by identity plus key, replacing any old value.
remember.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. key and value are runtime-required despite optional discovery schema. Kebab-case is descriptive guidance, not a schema pattern. Repeating the same key/value is logically idempotent; another value replaces the previous fact.
remember.summary: Save or replace a persistent fact by key.

remove_profile.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. A human operator may write directly; a caretaker must also have a live human-approved continuation whose action class is roster. Specialists and temporary agents are refused before configuration changes.
remove_profile.effects: Removes a profile, reloads the roster and records a feed entry.
remove_profile.notes: name is required. Refused while any configured routine still uses the profile; reassign those routines first. Does not remove routine notebooks or workspaces.
remove_profile.summary: Remove a profile that no routine currently uses.

remove_routine.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. A human operator may write directly; a caretaker must also have a live human-approved continuation whose action class is roster. Specialists and temporary agents are refused before configuration changes.
remove_routine.effects: Removes the routine configuration, reloads the roster, stops its live agent and records a feed entry. Notebook and workspace records remain.
remove_routine.notes: id is required. Removal also applies to external-tagged routines. It is not deletion of the routine's history or files; a later repeated removal may be refused as unknown. Sensors that target the removed ID remain configured for later cleanup.
remove_routine.result: id, path of configuration file, live=true.
remove_routine.summary: Remove a routine and stop its live agent.

repo_comment.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Served repositories only. Repository writes check the caller's active grant; observe mode logs violations, enforce mode refuses them. Operators bypass this grant check. Repository policy still applies.
repo_comment.effects: Posts a GitHub issue/PR comment and records repository-write activity.
repo_comment.notes: repo, number and body are required. Each successful repeat can create another comment; there is no deduplication key. Successful repo_verb activity is attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that supplies the shared repository process and policy.
repo_comment.result: repo, number and url of created comment.
repo_comment.summary: Post a comment on an issue or pull request.

repo_disown_pr.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. The repository must be served. A routine may act only on the repository in its current roster entry and is recorded as the owner. The human operator may act on any served repository and override record ownership.
repo_disown_pr.effects: Creates a local disownment record, changing how failing PR checks reach the operator. No GitHub write.
repo_disown_pr.notes: repo and number are required; reason is optional. Idempotent by repo+number for the record owner or operator: an existing record preserves its original author and reason. Another routine cannot revise that record. Authorization is checked before inserting a record.
repo_disown_pr.result: repo, number, disowned_by, reason and explanatory note.
repo_disown_pr.summary: Record that a pull request is outside the fleet work being handled.

repo_draft_issues.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
repo_draft_issues.effects: Stores a local batch of proposed issues. Does not write GitHub and does not itself create an approval gate.
repo_draft_issues.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. repo and issues are schema-required. Batch size is 1 through 25; every title must be nonblank, and each body is at most 20000 bytes. A retry creates another batch. Raise one permission gate naming the returned batch before filing it.
repo_draft_issues.result: batch_id, repo, drafted array of id/title/labels, and next-step instruction.
repo_draft_issues.summary: Prepare a local batch of issues for operator review.

repo_file_drafts.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity. The file_drafts grant check also applies, and each remote issue creation uses served-repository policy.
repo_file_drafts.effects: Creates GitHub issues for still-drafted entries, updates each local entry status and records a feed summary. Individual failure does not stop the remainder.
repo_file_drafts.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. batch_id is required. Unknown or foreign batches fail. Already-filed and already-failed entries are skipped on subsequent calls; results describe newly filed/failed entries plus dropped entries, not the full batch history. This is retry-safe for recorded completion, not a guarantee against an uncertain remote write before local persistence. Each successful per-issue repo_verb and the batch summary are attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that owns the batch or supplies the shared repository process and policy. An operator filing a routine-owned batch is therefore recorded as operator.
repo_file_drafts.result: batch_id; filed array of title/url; dropped array of titles; failed array of title/error.
repo_file_drafts.summary: File the kept issues from a reviewed local batch.

repo_list_issues.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Repository must be served by a configured routine. No caller ownership check or write-grant check. Reads do not emit repository-write feed entries.
repo_list_issues.notes: repo is required. state defaults to open; documented values are open, closed and all but are not schema enums. Issues are oldest-created first; PRs and ignore-labeled issues are removed. Ignore label defaults to custode:ignore. No pagination controls are exposed, so do not infer exhaustive results beyond upstream page behavior.
repo_list_issues.result: repo, issues array, ignored count and ignore_label.
repo_list_issues.summary: List issues the fleet should consider in a served repository.

repo_list_prs.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Repository must be served by a configured routine. No caller ownership check or write-grant check. Reads do not emit repository-write feed entries.
repo_list_prs.notes: repo is required. state defaults to open; documented values are open, closed and all without a schema enum. Oldest-created first. No pagination controls are exposed. GitHub mergeability fields may be null while computed.
repo_list_prs.result: repo and prs array; each PR has number, title, state, draft, base/base_sha, head/head_sha, mergeable, mergeable_state, merged, merged_at, merge_commit_sha, updated_at and url.
repo_list_prs.summary: List pull requests in a served repository.

repo_mark_issue_blocked.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Served repositories only. Repository writes check the caller's active grant; observe mode logs violations, enforce mode refuses them. Operators bypass this grant check. Repository policy still applies.
repo_mark_issue_blocked.effects: Posts 'blocked: <reason>' to the GitHub issue and records repository-write activity. Does not set an issue label.
repo_mark_issue_blocked.notes: repo, number and reason are required. Uses mark_issue, outside every bounded approval class; enforce mode therefore requires an unbounded grant. Repeats create additional comments. Successful repo_verb activity is attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that supplies the shared repository process and policy.
repo_mark_issue_blocked.result: repo, number and url of marker comment.
repo_mark_issue_blocked.summary: Post an issue blockage marker with its reason.

repo_mark_issue_ready.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Served repositories only. Repository writes check the caller's active grant; observe mode logs violations, enforce mode refuses them. Operators bypass this grant check. Repository policy still applies.
repo_mark_issue_ready.effects: Posts 'ready: <plan>' to the GitHub issue and records repository-write activity. Does not set an issue label.
repo_mark_issue_ready.notes: repo, number and plan are required. Uses the mark_issue grant verb, which belongs to no bounded approval class; enforce mode therefore requires an unbounded grant. Repeats create additional comments. Successful repo_verb activity is attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that supplies the shared repository process and policy.
repo_mark_issue_ready.result: repo, number and url of marker comment.
repo_mark_issue_ready.summary: Post an issue readiness marker with its plan.

repo_merge_pr.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Served repositories only. Repository writes check the caller's active grant; observe mode logs violations, enforce mode refuses them. Operators bypass this grant check. Repository policy still applies.
repo_merge_pr.effects: Requests a GitHub merge and records repository-write activity if repository policy and the review floor permit it.
repo_merge_pr.notes: repo and number are required. Shipped manual merge policy normally refuses this tool. Review evidence is also required, and a latest needs-human marker blocks it. This tool does not accept an expected head SHA or expose the separate head-checked merge-gate path. An explicit :merge_method Custode policy scoped to the served repository selects merge, squash or rebase and takes precedence over the default flag order, but GitHub must still allow that method. Without one, the repository's allow_merge_commit, allow_squash_merge and allow_rebase_merge flags select merge, then squash, then rebase; when all three flags are absent it sends the configured method or "merge". A repository that allows none of them, or disallows the configured method, is refused with a typed "policy merge_method: ..." error before any merge request. Selection happens after the merge-policy and review-floor checks. The separate exact-head merge Gate pins this selection, rechecks that exact method immediately before mutation, and records the method actually sent. Successful repo_verb activity is attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that supplies the shared repository process and policy.
repo_merge_pr.result: repo, number, state='merged' and merge_method (the method sent to GitHub) on accepted success.
repo_merge_pr.summary: Request a pull-request merge subject to repository policy.

repo_open_issue.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Served repositories only. Repository writes check the caller's active grant; observe mode logs violations, enforce mode refuses them. Operators bypass this grant check. Repository policy still applies.
repo_open_issue.effects: Creates a GitHub issue with optional labels and records repository-write activity.
repo_open_issue.notes: repo and title are required. body defaults to empty; labels pass through. Conventional title policy is checked. No idempotency key; an uncertain response can require checking GitHub before retry. Successful repo_verb activity is attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that supplies the shared repository process and policy.
repo_open_issue.summary: Create an issue in a served repository.

repo_open_pr.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Served repositories only. Repository writes check the caller's active grant; observe mode logs violations, enforce mode refuses them. Operators bypass this grant check. Repository policy still applies.
repo_open_pr.effects: Creates a GitHub pull request, always as a draft, and records repository-write activity.
repo_open_pr.notes: repo, title and head are required. base defaults to main; body defaults to empty. Conventional title policy is checked. Does not create or push the head branch. No idempotency key; do not blindly retry after an uncertain remote result. Successful repo_verb activity is attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that supplies the shared repository process and policy.
repo_open_pr.summary: Create a draft pull request in a served repository.

repo_pr_checks.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Repository must be served by a configured routine. No caller ownership check or write-grant check. Reads do not emit repository-write feed entries.
repo_pr_checks.effects: None; fetches the current PR head and its GitHub check runs.
repo_pr_checks.notes: repo and number are required. sha identifies the head observed by this call. This is check-run data, not a promise to aggregate every GitHub status-context mechanism; pagination controls are not exposed.
repo_pr_checks.result: repo, sha and checks array: id, name, status, conclusion, url, started_at, completed_at.
repo_pr_checks.summary: Read check runs for the current pull-request head.

repo_pr_diff.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Repository must be served by a configured routine. No caller ownership check or write-grant check. Reads do not emit repository-write feed entries.
repo_pr_diff.effects: None; fetches changed-file metadata and patches from GitHub.
repo_pr_diff.notes: repo and number are required. previous_filename and patch may be null or absent upstream, including binary/large changes. No pagination controls are exposed; it is not a guaranteed complete local diff.
repo_pr_diff.result: repo and files array: filename, previous_filename, status, additions, deletions and patch.
repo_pr_diff.summary: Read changed-file metadata and patches for a pull request.

repo_ready_pr.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Served repositories only. Repository writes check the caller's active grant; observe mode logs violations, enforce mode refuses them. Operators bypass this grant check. Repository policy still applies.
repo_ready_pr.effects: Changes a GitHub draft PR to ready for review and records repository-write activity.
repo_ready_pr.notes: repo and number are required. Uses GitHub's ready-for-review operation; this is not a merge or an approval review. Remote refusal is a tool error. Successful repo_verb activity is attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that supplies the shared repository process and policy.
repo_ready_pr.summary: Mark a draft pull request ready for review.

repo_reclaim_pr.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. The repository must be served. A routine may act only on its configured repository and may reclaim only a record it owns. The human operator may reclaim any record in any served repository.
repo_reclaim_pr.effects: Deletes the local disownment record so future failing-check attention returns to normal fleet handling. No GitHub write.
repo_reclaim_pr.notes: repo and number are required. Missing disownment is an error ('was not disowned'), so a completed repeat is not a successful no-op. Repository and owner authorization occurs before deletion.

repo_review_pr.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Served repositories only. Repository writes check the caller's active grant; observe mode logs violations, enforce mode refuses them. Operators bypass this grant check. Repository policy still applies.
repo_review_pr.effects: Posts a 'review: <verdict> -- <body>' GitHub comment used by Custode's merge review floor. Does not submit a formal GitHub review.
repo_review_pr.notes: repo, number, verdict and body are required. Schema prose suggests lgtm or needs-human, but the implementation accepts other verdict strings. Exact needs-human blocks merging until superseded by later qualifying review evidence; other marker text counts as reviewed. Repeats create comments. Successful repo_verb activity is attributed to the authenticated MCP caller, independent of the routine that supplies the shared repository process and policy.
repo_review_pr.result: repo, number, verdict and url of marker comment.
repo_review_pr.summary: Record a review marker used by the merge policy.

repo_view_issue.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Repository must be served by a configured routine. No caller ownership check or write-grant check. Reads do not emit repository-write feed entries.
repo_view_issue.effects: None; fetches GitHub issue and comments.
repo_view_issue.notes: repo and number are required. Ignore-label filtering does not apply to an explicit issue read. Comment pagination is not exposed.
repo_view_issue.result: repo plus issue number, title, state, labels, updated_at, url, body and comments. Each comment has id, author, body, created_at, updated_at.
repo_view_issue.summary: Read one issue and its comments.

repo_view_pr.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Repository must be served by a configured routine. No caller ownership check or write-grant check. Reads do not emit repository-write feed entries.
repo_view_pr.effects: None; fetches a GitHub pull request.
repo_view_pr.notes: repo and number are required. This result does not include reviews, comments or checks; obtain checks/diff separately. Mergeability fields may be null.
repo_view_pr.result: repo plus the PR fields returned by repo_list_prs, and body.
repo_view_pr.summary: Read one pull request and its current branch information.

resume_agent.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. The shared operator action repeats that boundary, so specialists, temporary agents and alternate clients are refused before agent state changes.
resume_agent.effects: Resumes a paused agent, including an operator override of a budget pause.
resume_agent.notes: agent_id is required. Failed transitions return 'resume failed'. It does not increase budget settings or undo effects from before the pause.

run_job.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. A routine is limited to its configured working directory or deterministic owned checkout and its own notebook inbox. Elevated routine jobs require a live approved continuation whose action class permits shell work. The human operator may use any existing directories and run elevated jobs directly. Any caller may lower max_turns; raising it above the default requires the operator or a routine with a live approved continuation whose action class permits shell work, the same rule as elevated jobs. That approved action's text must also name the cap with one stable max_turns=<N> marker, and a raised request must equal N exactly, so the approved gate detail names the resolved cap; a missing marker, more than one distinct marker, or a raised request other than N is refused.
run_job.effects: Enqueues a one-shot Claude run that can edit files, spend model budget, and write a completion note. Elevated jobs have full shell/Git/GitHub permissions.
run_job.notes: prompt and report_inbox are required; report_inbox and any workspace must already be directories. A routine that omits workspace uses its configured working directory. Lexical and physical path containment prevent traversal and symlink escapes. Path and elevation checks occur before a job is inserted. model and max_budget_usd default to configuration; tag defaults to 'job'. max_turns defaults to run_job_max_turns (15). A named max_turns must be a positive integer no greater than run_job_max_turns_ceiling (150); invalid, zero, over-ceiling or unauthorized values are tool errors and no job is inserted. The configured bounds are validated on every call, including an omitted max_turns: both must be positive integers and the default may not exceed the ceiling, or the call is a tool error and no job is inserted. Runs have a 200000 ms timeout, or 900000 ms when elevated. The completion note's custode-report header carries the resolved max_turns, and a failure note names the turn cap. Acceptance is asynchronous and not idempotent. Final report requires status and summary, with optional artifacts array and cost_note.
run_job.result: job_id, absolute reports_to directory and the resolved max_turns.
run_job.summary: Queue a bounded one-shot task with an inbox completion report.

set_next_beat.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
set_next_beat.effects: Upserts a one-shot scheduling request and records a feed entry. Cron beats are skipped until the requested due time; a started turn clears it.
set_next_beat.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. minutes and reason are runtime-required. minutes must be an integer and is clamped to configured bounds, default 5 through 1440. The reply reports the granted time. Operator messages, sensors, inbox events, immediate beats or approvals can start work sooner and clear it. Scheduler availability and other lifecycle rules still apply; this is not an unconditional delivery guarantee. Retrying computes a new deadline relative to the retry time and replaces the previous request.
set_next_beat.result: next_beat_at timestamp, granted minutes and clamped boolean.
set_next_beat.summary: Request a bounded one-shot change to the next scheduled sweep.

set_panel.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity. Refused when panels are off.
set_panel.effects: Appends a panel version and records a feed event. Approved HTML renders in the dashboard's sandboxed frame.
set_panel.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. html is runtime-required. Maximum is 20000 bytes. Gated mode is the default; auto mode approves immediately, so approval is not unconditional. Inline SVG/CSS can render; scripts do not run in the frame. Retrying creates another version.
set_panel.result: status: pending in gated mode or approved in auto mode.
set_panel.summary: Propose a dashboard panel for a routine.

set_presence.access: Main endpoint capability: human operator only. The shared operator action repeats the human-only boundary and refuses every routine and temporary agent before changing presence.
set_presence.effects: Pins operator presence to present/away, or restores automatic inference and records a fresh operator action.
set_presence.notes: mode is required and runtime-validated as present, away or auto. It influences instructions agents read; it does not itself pause the scheduler or approve work.
set_presence.result: mode and reading of effective presence state.
set_presence.summary: Set or release an operator-presence override.

spend_today.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. Specialists and temporary agents are refused. The handler has no narrower caller-identity check.
spend_today.notes: No arguments. Today starts at midnight in configured fleet timezone, not necessarily UTC. since identifies the counted boundary. Missing cost telemetry must not be inferred from a zero total alone.
spend_today.result: since, timezone, routines array of agent_id/today_usd/daily_budget_usd/today_tokens/daily_budget_tokens, fleet_today_usd and fleet_today_tokens.
spend_today.summary: Read fleet and per-routine spend for the current local day.

start_agent.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. A routine may start a new temporary identity or restart its recorded child, but cannot use a configured routine ID or take over another parent's child. The operator may override target scope. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint and by the shared delegation check.
start_agent.effects: Mints sub-agent credentials and writes its MCP config, starts a persistent agent process, and records parent/spawn metadata. Does not submit a prompt.
start_agent.notes: agent_id and workspace are required. workspace must exist and is expanded to an absolute path. model defaults to configuration. The child has a 240000 ms turn timeout and elevated approved continuations. Retry is not idempotent: credentials/config are written before the start result. Errors include a nonexistent workspace and 'start failed'.
start_agent.summary: Start a persistent helper agent in an existing directory.

todo_add.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Authenticated agents may write only their own records; the operator may name any identity.
todo_add.effects: Inserts an open todo, regenerates notebook views and notifies the dashboard.
todo_add.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. text is runtime-required despite optional discovery schema. Retrying adds another todo.

todo_complete.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Looks up the todo owner; agents may complete only their own, while the operator may complete any.
todo_complete.effects: Marks an existing todo done, regenerates notebook views and notifies the dashboard.
todo_complete.notes: todo_id is required. Unknown IDs fail with 'no todo #<id>'. Completing an already done todo keeps it done but still performs bookkeeping.

todo_list.access: Main endpoint capability: operator, caretaker, or specialist routine. Temporary agents are refused at the endpoint. Any authenticated caller reaching this tool may read another identity's todos by ID; no self-only read guard.
todo_list.notes: routine_id takes precedence over agent_id; either defaults to the authenticated agent. Operators must supply an identity. Blank identity strings count as absent. status defaults open and is runtime-validated as open, done or all. Oldest todo ID first. No limit input.
todo_list.result: todos array of id, text and status.
todo_list.summary: Read open, completed or all todos for an identity.

update_profile.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. A human operator may write directly; a caretaker must also have a live human-approved continuation whose action class is roster. Specialists and temporary agents are refused before configuration changes.
update_profile.effects: Rewrites the profile, reloads the roster and records a feed entry. Routines inheriting it receive the change on their next run. If the effective provider changes, live wearers are stopped on the old provider and restart on their next beat.
update_profile.notes: name is required. provider is claude or codex. Omitted fields remain unchanged; drop removes envelope keys, lists replace, and false bypass does not explicitly revoke an existing grant. Preview the resulting approved_args before writing. Supplying any approve_* values replaces the approved_args envelope rather than merging nested keys. Rewriting removes comments inside the edited section.
update_profile.result: name, configuration path and live=true. Unlike define_profile, this result does not include grants.

update_routine.access: Main endpoint capability: operator or caretaker routine. A human operator may write directly; a caretaker must also have a live human-approved continuation whose action class is roster. Specialists and temporary agents are refused before configuration changes.
update_routine.effects: Rewrites configuration, reloads the live roster and records changed field names in the feed. Updated schedule is used by subsequent scheduler checks. A provider change stops the live agent on the old provider; the next beat starts it on the new provider. A repository change starts service for the new repository and can retire the old service if no longer needed.
update_routine.notes: id is required and immutable. provider is claude or codex. Omitted fields stay unchanged; lists replace; drop removes overrides and wins over a supplied value. Preview before applying. This response does not promise changes to an already executing turn. Rewriting removes comments inside the edited configuration section; comments in other sections are preserved.
update_routine.result: id, path of configuration file, live=true.
